content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 先声药业拿下凌科药业泽普昔替尼皮肤科独家商业化权益，国产JAK1抑制剂特应性皮炎NDA获受理 先声药业拿下凌科药业泽普昔替尼皮肤科独家商业化权益，国产JAK1抑制剂特应性皮炎NDA获受理 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 昨天 14:37 1658 JAK1 凌科药业（杭州）有限公司 特应性皮炎 江苏先声医药科技有限公司 强直性脊柱炎 11月2日，先声药业发布公告，宣布与凌科药业（浙江）股份有限公司达成新一轮合作，获得选择性JAK1抑制剂泽普昔替尼在中国大陆及港澳台地区，用于成人中重度特应性皮炎及其他皮肤科适应症的独家商业化权益。图源：先声药业企业公告这是双方继2022年3月首次合作后的再次携手。此前，先声药业已获得泽普昔替尼治疗类风湿关节炎、强直性脊柱炎两大适应症的大中华区独家商业化权益。本次合作进一步将商业化布局拓展至皮肤科领域。值得关注的是，泽普昔替尼治疗中重度特应性皮炎的关键性Ⅲ期临床研究已完成，相关新药上市申请（NDA）于2026年4月获国家药监局药品审评中心（CDE）受理。一、二度合作，商业化权益再扩容泽普昔替尼由凌科药业自主研发，是一款高选择性、口服第二代JAK1抑制剂，正在开发用于类风湿关节炎、特应性皮炎及强直性脊柱炎等炎症和自身免疫性疾病。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库此次合作是双方2022年首次合作后的进一步扩容。先声药业在原有风湿免疫适应症商业化权益基础上，新增获得泽普昔替尼在特应性皮炎及其他皮肤科适应症的独家商业化权益。摩熵医药数据库显示，目前，JAK3抑制剂SIM-0280也在布局自身免疫性疾病领域，尚处于临床前研究阶段。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库对于先声药业而言，此次合作有望进一步丰富自身免疫领域产品组合，并利用现有商业化体系推进产品市场开发；对于凌科药业而言，则可以借助先声药业的商业化能力，为产品后续上市及市场推广提供支持。双方此次合作的具体交易金额、里程碑付款及销售分成比例尚未披露。二、III期临床完成，特应性皮炎上市申请获受理临床数据方面，泽普昔替尼治疗中重度特应性皮炎的Ⅲ期研究共纳入356例患者。结果显示，治疗第16周时，两个剂量组在EASI-75、vIGA-AD 0/1及瘙痒改善等终点上均显著优于安慰剂组。起效时间方面，给药后第1天即可观察到瘙痒改善，第2周开始出现皮损改善。安全性方面，不良事件以轻中度为主，严重不良事件和特别关注不良事件发生率与安慰剂组基本相当，未发现新的安全性信号。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库除特应性皮炎外，泽普昔替尼治疗类风湿关节炎的Ⅲ期临床研究已完成，针对强直性脊柱炎的Ⅲ期临床开发项目仍在进行中。目前，特应性皮炎领域已有度普利尤单抗等生物制剂，以及乌帕替尼、阿布昔替尼等口服JAK抑制剂。泽普昔替尼未来若顺利获批，仍需面对较为充分的市场竞争，其疗效、安全性及长期用药表现将成为影响市场竞争力的重要因素。从首次合作到权益扩容，先声药业与凌科药业进一步深化泽普昔替尼的商业化合作。随着特应性皮炎适应症进入上市申请审评阶段，这款国产口服JAK1抑制剂的后续进展值得关注。参考来源：[1] 授予安斯泰来获得DAX-044全球开发与商业化许可的独家选择权，Audax保留在澳大利亚和新西兰共同出资、联合推广DAX-044的选择权 Audax将出资并继续推进DAX-044开发直至Ⅰ期临床 交易总潜在价值最高可达13.4亿美元（不含特许权使用费）日本东京、澳大利亚墨尔本，2026年10月28日——安斯泰来制药株式会社（TSE: 4503，社长兼CEO：冈村直树，以下简称"安斯泰来"）与Audax Biosciences Pty Ltd（"Audax"）今日宣布，双方已就DAX-044签署独家选择权与许可协议。DAX-044是Audax核心的肿瘤免疫AVIKINE®候选药物。根据协议，安斯泰来获得一项独家选择权，行权后将获得DAX-044的全球开发、生产与商业化许可。Audax保留在澳大利亚和新西兰共同出资、联合推广DAX-044的选择权。该协议进一步强化了安斯泰来在肿瘤免疫领域的研发管线——肿瘤免疫是安斯泰来研发战略的核心聚焦领域之一——并与其靶向免疫疗法产品组合形成互补。安斯泰来首席战略官Takahiko Iwaya"在安斯泰来，我们致力于推进有望解决癌症患者显著未满足需求的创新疗法。DAX-044是一个极具前景的肿瘤免疫在研项目，其差异化的作用机制可选择性激活抗肿瘤免疫应答。通过将Audax的创新科学与安斯泰来的开发、生产和商业化专长相结合，我们希望为实体瘤患者——包括有效免疫刺激仍是重要治疗难题的那些癌症——推进一种潜在的新治疗选择。”Audax Biosciences首席执行官，博士、MBA Jai Rautela"安斯泰来与我们在肿瘤免疫领域的开拓精神高度契合，是DAX-044这类高度差异化项目的理想合作伙伴。这一合作将加速DAX-044按计划开展的Ⅰ期临床评估，惠及多种实体瘤患者。本次交易体现了对我们新型疗法开发路径的信心，也展现了在我们本土市场共同开发DAX-044的潜力。”DAX-044是一款在研的免疫靶向白介素-12（IL-12）抗体-细胞因子融合蛋白，基于AVIKINE®技术设计，可将IL-12的免疫激活活性富集于肿瘤微环境内部，同时限制历来制约IL-12疗法的全身性毒性。临床前研究显示，DAX-044在IL-12类药物中具备同类最优的潜在治疗指数，目前正处于IND/CTN申报支持性开发阶段。根据协议条款，Audax将获得首付款及潜在的未来选择权行权款，合计2.85亿美元，并继续推进DAX-044的开发，预计2027年开展Ⅰ期临床研究。安斯泰来行权后，将全权负责DAX-044的全球开发、生产与商业化，Audax则可选择在澳大利亚和新西兰共同出资、联合推广DAX-044。此外，若DAX-044获批上市，Audax还有资格获得最高10.5亿美元的开发及商业化里程碑付款，以及按全球净销售额计算的阶梯式两位数特许权使用费。选择权的行使须满足惯例性条件，包括获得相关反垄断审批。关于安斯泰来安斯泰来是一家全球生命科学企业，致力于将创新科学转化为患者的价值。我们在肿瘤、眼科、泌尿、免疫及女性健康等疾病领域提供变革性疗法。通过研发项目，我们正为存在高度未满足医疗需求的疾病开拓新的医疗解决方案。了解更多信息，请访问：www.astellas.com关于Audax BiosciencesAudax Biosciences是一家澳大利亚生物技术公司，致力于开发针对癌症及其他免疫相关疾病的下一代免疫疗法。我们为最急需的免疫学难题开发新颖解决方案，为现有药物未能充分覆盖的患者带来希望。我们的临床前产品组合还包括更多AVIKINE®项目以及其他针对每种目标疾病量身定制、尚未公开的药物形式。更多信息请访问：www.audax.bio安斯泰来提示性说明在本新闻稿中，有关当前计划、估计、战略和信念的陈述以及其他非历史事实的陈述，均为关于安斯泰来未来业绩的前瞻性陈述。这些陈述基于管理层根据现有信息作出的当前假设和信念，涉及已知和未知的风险与不确定性。多种因素可能导致实际结果与前瞻性陈述中讨论的内容出现重大差异。这些因素包括但不限于：（i）总体经济环境以及与药品市场相关的法律法规的变化；（ii）汇率波动；（iii）新产品上市延迟；（iv）安斯泰来无法有效销售现有产品和新产品；（v）在竞争激烈的市场中，安斯泰来无法继续有效研发客户认可的产品；以及（vi）安斯泰来的知识产权受到第三方侵犯。本新闻稿中包含的药品信息（包括目前在研产品）不构成广告或医疗建议。+++1.本文翻译自安斯泰来全球新闻稿，原文链接为：Astellas title: 石药集团牵手康方生物：B7-H3 ADC SYS6043联合PD-1/VEGF双抗依沃西，国内联合疗法临床正式启动
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 石药集团牵手康方生物：B7-H3 ADC SYS6043联合PD-1/VEGF双抗依沃西，国内联合疗法临床正式启动 石药集团牵手康方生物：B7-H3 ADC SYS6043联合PD-1/VEGF双抗依沃西，国内联合疗法临床正式启动 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 昨天 15:05 1900 PD-1 中山康方生物医药有限公司 石药集团有限公司 VEGF CD276 11月2日，石药集团与康方生物宣布达成临床合作，双方将围绕石药自主研发的B7-H3 ADC（SYS6043）与康方PD-1/VEGF双抗依沃西注射液开展联合开发，合作区域为中国大陆，相关临床试验成果由双方共同所有。图源：石药集团企业官微ADC与免疫疗法联合开发并不新鲜，但此次合作有一个值得关注的细节：石药选择的不是传统PD-1单抗，而是同时靶向PD-1和VEGF的双抗依沃西。这也释放出一个信号：随着ADC联合疗法不断推进，PD-1/VEGF双抗正成为创新药企业探索ADC联合治疗的新选择。一、B7-H3 ADC联手PD-1/VEGF双抗SYS6043由石药巨石生物自主研发，是一款靶向B7-H3的新一代ADC，采用拓扑异构酶I抑制剂作为载荷，DAR约为6，采用Fcγ受体效应沉默设计以降低脱靶毒性，具有可裂解连接子和旁观者效应。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库临床数据方面，2026年ESMO公布的乳腺癌队列数据显示，在139例患者中，TNBC、HR+/HER2-及HER2+亚组的确认客观缓解率（ORR）分别达到75.0%、53.7%和69.6%；3级及以上治疗期间不良事件发生率为28.8%，间质性肺病发生率为1.4%。此外，2026年ASCO公布的全瘤种I/II期研究数据显示，533例可评估患者整体ORR为41.8%，其中肺癌和乳腺癌亚组ORR分别为46.3%和56.8%。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库此次合作的另一款药——依沃西，是康方生物自主研发的PD-1/VEGF双特异性抗体，目前已获批3项适应症。在临床研究中，依沃西已展现出一定的头对头竞争优势。例如，HARMONi-6研究中，依沃西联合化疗一线治疗鳞状非小细胞肺癌，中位总生存期（mOS）达到27.9个月，对照组为23.7个月；HARMONi-2研究中，依沃西单药一线治疗PD-L1阳性非小细胞肺癌，mOS达到30.8个月，对照组为22.6个月。值得注意的是，此次石药选择依沃西作为SYS6043的联合开发搭档，而非简单采用传统PD-1单抗，也让这笔合作有了更多值得关注的地方。二、ADC联合疗法，竞争逻辑正在变化为什么PD-1/VEGF双抗开始受到ADC研发企业关注？传统PD-1抑制剂主要通过解除T细胞的免疫抑制状态发挥作用，而VEGF除了促进肿瘤血管生成，还参与肿瘤免疫微环境的调节。因此，PD-1/VEGF双抗能够同时作用于免疫检查点和VEGF通路，有望改善肿瘤免疫微环境，为ADC联合治疗提供新的协同思路。简单来说，ADC负责靶向递送细胞毒载荷、杀伤肿瘤细胞，VEGF阻断有望改善免疫抑制微环境，PD-1阻断则帮助恢复T细胞抗肿瘤活性。三种作用机制存在潜在互补性。这一方向已经吸引多家药企布局。康方生物此前披露，阿斯利康、GSK、辉瑞、吉利德等跨国药企，以及国内多家ADC企业，均已开展核心ADC产品与依沃西的联合疗法探索。此外，BNT324/DB-1311联合PD-L1/VEGF双抗Pumitamig，以及科伦博泰B7-H3 ADC SKB500联合自研PD-1/VEGF双抗SKB118，也在推进相关联合治疗探索。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库这意味着，ADC与PD-1/VEGF双抗的联合开发正在成为值得关注的研发方向。对于康方生物而言，依沃西与多家ADC企业建立合作，有望进一步拓展其联合治疗布局，积累不同靶点、不同瘤种的临床数据。对于石药集团而言，此次合作则为SYS6043增加了一种新的联合治疗开发路径。从单一药物研发到联合治疗探索，ADC赛道的竞争正在延伸至联合搭档的选择。依沃西能否凭借已有临床数据和不断扩大的合作网络，形成差异化竞争优势，仍有待后续临床研究验证。 title: AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 15, 2026 AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff AstraZeneca will pay insitro $40 million upfront to apply AI to target discovery in MASH and cardiomyopathies, with no candidates named yet. Advertisement AstraZeneca has signed a drug discovery collaboration and licensing agreement with insitro to apply artificial intelligence (AI) to target identification and therapeutic design in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and cardiomyopathies, the companies announced Oct. 15.1,2 Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in milestones.1,2Sharon Barr, executive vice president and head of BioPharmaceuticals research and development at AstraZeneca, tied the agreement to target selection: “We know that disease biology is incredibly complex, and one of the most critical decisions in R&D is selecting the right target. This strategic collaboration underscores our commitment to maximizing the potential of cutting-edge AI to tackle the root cause of disease. Partnering with insitro, we will use advanced AI to identify the biological drivers of disease to support the rapid discovery of high-quality novel targets, advancing our ambition to deliver the next generation of medicines to patients faster.”1“MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. title: Novartis Exits BrainTransporter Deal with BioArctic 14 Months After Signing
content: Advertisement News|Articles|November 3, 2026 Novartis Exits BrainTransporter Deal with BioArctic 14 Months After Signing Novartis exits its BrainTransporter deal with BioArctic 14 months after signing, citing an internal portfolio decision unrelated to the platform. Advertisement Novartis has terminated its collaboration with BioArctic AB, ending a partnership designed to use BioArctic’s BrainTransporter platform to develop a new treatment for neurodegenerative disorders1 — just 14 months after the two companies signed the agreement.2BioArctic announced the termination on November 2, 2026. The Swedish biotech said Novartis decided to discontinue the program, and was clear that the exit reflects an internal Novartis portfolio decision rather than any problem with the platform itself. “The termination is unrelated to BioArctic’s BrainTransporter technology,” the company stated.The collaboration, inked in August 2025, had called for BioArctic to engineer a drug candidate by pairing BrainTransporter with an undisclosed Novartis proprietary antibody targeting neurodegeneration. Novartis would then evaluate the resulting data and decide whether to exercise an option to license the candidate and take over global development and commercialization. The deal carried an upfront payment of $30 million, with up to $772 million in potential milestone payments and tiered mid-single-digit royalties on global sales if a product reached the market. For example, a citizen’s petition filed in late October asked the FDA to, for safety reasons, require regular monitoring of antibody levels for patients taking the drug, as well as guidance for managing low levels. Two similar medicines are already available, too. Additionally, Vertex wants to provide pove as a highly concentrated, low volume shot delivered about once a month via an at-home autoinjector. Developing and scaling the manufacturing for that kind of product is often challenging. Still, Vertex executives affirmed their conviction. With the FDA’s decision deadline fast-approaching, “we are 100% ready” to sell the product and “are incredibly excited to bring pove to patients,” McKechnie said. The company “essentially gave bulls what they wanted to hear,” wrote Carter Gould, an analyst at Cantor Fitzgerald, in a note to clients. “Given that this was arguably one of the last opportunities to potentially reset expectations around approval or the label ahead of the [decision deadline], management's repeated expressions of confidence should be viewed as strongly encouraging,” Gould added. Earlier this year, when Vertex reported key late-stage data for pove, Gould described the results as “the first major step” to unlocking a renal franchise that could exceed $10 billion in peak annual sales. Such a franchise would go “a long way toward differentiating Vertex’s growth profile [versus its] larger-cap peers.” Another core piece of that franchise is inaxaplin, which is in testing as a treatment for kidney disease caused by mutations in a gene called APOL1. Analysts noted that Vertex leadership sounded confident in an upcoming trial readout for inaxaplin — another “potentially major catalyst” for the company’s stock, according to Christopher Raymond of Raymond James. content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 益方生物TYK2抑制剂Nomelcitinib银屑病III期成功，多自身免疫适应症同步推进 益方生物TYK2抑制剂Nomelcitinib银屑病III期成功，多自身免疫适应症同步推进 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 昨天 14:05 2047 TYK2 银屑病 IL-23R D-2570片 益方生物科技（上海）股份有限公司 11月2日，益方生物宣布，自主研发的TYK2抑制剂 Nomelcitinib（D-2570）治疗中重度斑块状银屑病的注册性III期临床研究达到主要终点和关键次要终点。图源：益方生物企业公告研究结果显示，该药治疗第16周时PASI 90达标率超过70%，PGA 0/1达标率超过80%，且治疗第4周就已显示出显著疗效。这意味着Nomelcitinib在银屑病领域的临床开发取得重要进展。一、III期研究成功，起效仅需4周Nomelcitinib是益方生物自主研发的一款新型口服选择性TYK2抑制剂，通过选择性结合TYK2假激酶域（JH2），抑制TYK2激酶活性，阻断TYK2依赖性的细胞因子信号传导，从而参与免疫调节。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库此次III期研究是一项多中心、随机、双盲、安慰剂对照临床试验，共纳入391例中重度斑块状银屑病患者，旨在评价Nomelcitinib的有效性和安全性。研究主要终点为治疗第16周时达到PASI 90（银屑病面积与严重程度指数较基线改善至少90%）的患者比例；关键次要终点为达到PGA 0/1（皮损完全清除或几乎完全清除，且较基线下降至少2分）的患者比例。结果显示，治疗第16周时，两个Nomelcitinib治疗组的PASI 90达标率均超过70%，PGA 0/1达标率均超过80%，两项指标均显著优于安慰剂组。值得关注的是，Nomelcitinib起效较快。治疗第4周时，两个治疗组达到PASI 90和PGA 0/1的患者比例便已显著高于安慰剂组，且随着治疗时间延长，疗效进一步提升。在其他次要疗效终点分析中，Nomelcitinib治疗组同样优于安慰剂组，差异具有统计学意义。安全性方面，Nomelcitinib整体表现出良好的安全性和耐受性，其安全性特征与既往II期临床研究及其他选择性TYK2 JH2抑制剂相似，未发现新的安全性信号。二、多适应症布局持续推进，临床数据展现竞争潜力此次III期研究结果与此前II期研究数据保持高度一致，进一步支持了Nomelcitinib在银屑病领域的开发潜力。除此次注册性III期研究外，益方生物还在推进Nomelcitinib与氘可来昔替尼头对头比较的银屑病III期临床试验，以进一步评价其有效性和安全性。在其他适应症方面，公司正在开展Nomelcitinib治疗中重度活动性溃疡性结肠炎（UC）、银屑病关节炎（PsA）、系统性红斑狼疮（SLE）及白癜风等疾病的II期临床试验，同时也在美国开展该药治疗银屑病的II期临床试验。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库从已披露的临床数据来看，Nomelcitinib的疗效指标也展现出一定竞争力。以治疗第16周的PASI 90和PGA/IGA 0/1达标率为例，IL-23R拮抗剂伊可白滞素在三项III期研究中的相关数据如下：ICONIC-LEAD研究：第16周PASI 90达标率为49.6%，IGA 0/1达标率为64.7%。ICONIC-ADVANCE 1研究：第16周PASI 90达标率为55%，IGA 0/1达标率为68%。ICONIC-ADVANCE 2研究：第16周PASI 90达标率为57%，IGA 0/1达标率为70%。相比之下，Nomelcitinib两个治疗组的PASI 90达标率均超过70%，PGA 0/1达标率均超过80%，数值上高于上述伊可白滞素研究结果。需要注意的是，上述数据来自不同临床试验，研究设计、入组人群及评价标准可能存在差异，不能直接等同于头对头疗效比较。从研发进展来看，Nomelcitinib已从银屑病II期研究推进至注册性III期阶段，同时围绕多种自身免疫及炎症性疾病开展临床探索。随着银屑病头对头III期研究及其他适应症研究持续推进，其后续临床数据和开发进展值得关注。 Advertisement Karyopharm Therapeutics, the maker of the multiple myeloma treatment Xpovio (selinexor), filed for Chapter 11 protection on Nov. 2 under a restructuring support agreement that provides for a merger with Ayrmid, the parent company of Gamida Cell.1 The plan would convert roughly $276 million of funded debt into a majority stake in the combined company and cancel existing common and preferred shares without a distribution.2The company will seek court approval of bidding procedures that allow other parties to submit competing offers, with closing expected in the first quarter of 2027.1 “Following a comprehensive review of available alternatives, we believe this process provides a clear framework to pursue a value maximizing transaction for our stakeholders while continuing our important work of advancing therapies for patients with multiple myeloma and myelofibrosis,” said Richard Paulson, president and CEO of Karyopharm.1Key FactsDeal: Ayrmid merger through Chapter 11 planLead bidder: Ayrmid; rival bids allowedDebtor-in-possession financing: up to $55MDebt holders to receive 55% of combined companyExisting shareholders: no distributionProduct: Xpovio (selinexor), exportin 1 inhibitorTarget close: first quarter of 2027“We see considerable potential in Karyopharm’s marketed products, development pipeline and experienced team, and believe that, together, we can build a broader, stronger commercial-stage hematology business with meaningful opportunities for future growth.” — Dr. Joe Wiley, chairman and chief executive officer of AyrmidWhat are the proposed merger terms?Under the plan described in Karyopharm’s disclosure statement, which the court has not yet approved, creditors holding the roughly $276 million of funded debt would receive 55% of the combined company’s common stock, along with contingent value rights tied to future Xpovio sales in myelofibrosis.2 Ayrmid’s existing equity holders would receive the remaining 45% and contingent equity tied to future revenue from its product Omisirge.2 The combined company would emerge with no more than $135 million of funded debt, a reduction of about $141 million, and Karyopharm’s common stock is expected to be delisted from Nasdaq.2Karyopharm has secured commitments for up to $55 million in debtor-in-possession financing from existing secured lenders, which, with cash from operations, is expected to support the business during the case once the court approves it.1 The company says it expects ordinary operations and partnerships to continue without disruption.1 The market test remains open: if a rival bid meets conditions that include at least $335 million in net proceeds at closing, the company may pursue a sale instead of the merger.2Why did Karyopharm file for Chapter 11?The disclosure statement attributes the filing to sustained operating losses and a reliance on capital markets that depended on clinical progress.2 When two phase 3 readouts in 2026 fell short of expectations and liquidity tightened, secured creditors agreed to payment deferrals and forbearances.2 A formal sale process launched in July 2026 drew multiple proposals, none of which In the phase 3 SENTRY trial of 353 patients, 50% of those given selinexor plus ruxolitinib reached a spleen volume reduction of at least 35% at week 24, versus 28% with ruxolitinib alone, but the groups did not differ significantly on the symptom-score co-primary endpoint, according to company-reported topline results.4 Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 70% of patients on the combination and 50% on ruxolitinib alone.4 Karyopharm submitted a supplemental new drug application seeking accelerated approval on Aug. 31, 2026.2How does the merger fit hematology commercial strategy?Ayrmid markets two FDA-approved products in the United States: Omisirge (omidubicel-onlv), a cell therapy for certain hematologic malignancies and severe aplastic anemia, and Aphexda (motixafortide), which mobilizes hematopoietic stem cells in adults with multiple myeloma.1 Multiple myeloma is the point at which the two companies’ marketed products overlap. “We see a strong strategic fit between Ayrmid and Karyopharm, with complementary portfolios, established commercial capabilities and a shared commitment to addressing significant unmet needs in hematology,” said Dr. Joe Wiley, chairman and chief executive officer of Ayrmid.1What risks and open questions remain?The plan still requires court confirmation. Holders of all claims entitled to vote have agreed to support it, according to the filing, so uncertainty centers on court approval, rival bids and regulatory reviews.2 Creditor voting closes Nov. 30, and the company has asked for a hearing on Jan. 11, 2027.2 Antitrust and foreign investment reviews are under evaluation, while FDA approval of the transaction itself is not expected to be required.2Projections for the combined company will be filed later with a plan supplement, so the commercial case remains unquantified.2 No FDA decision on the myelofibrosis application is reported in the sources reviewed, and SENTRY’s mixed result leaves that program’s regulatory outcome unsettled.2SourcesKaryopharm Therapeutics Inc. announces planned merger with Ayrmid Ltd. to strengthen company for the future. Bristol Myers Squibb on Friday reported that one patient died after receiving its investigational CAR-T therapy in an early autoimmune trial, adding to safety concerns about a growing field of research. In a Phase 1 trial that tested the therapy in multiple sclerosis, a condition that causes muscle weakness and extreme fatigue, the patient experienced motor symptoms that did not resolve with standard autoimmune treatments. They were then given a potent immunosuppressant, but developed septic pneumonia and died, Bristol said in a press release.Advertisement In a subsequent statement sent to STAT, Bristol said this patient was treated for a series of other complications prior to receiving the CAR-T therapy, “confounding our ability to determine the root cause of the issue.” STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account? title: STAT Plus: Coming readout of Kymera eczema trial is a high-stakes moment in a bid to rival Dupixent
content: STAT PlusBiotech Coming readout of Kymera eczema trial is a high-stakes moment in a bid to rival Dupixent Biotech aspires to turn pill into a therapy for multiple immunology and inflammatory disorders Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Adobe By Jonathan WosenNov. 2, 2026 West Coast Biotech & Life Sciences Reporter Jonathan Wosen[email protected]Jonathan Wosen is STAT’s West Coast biotech & life sciences reporter. You can reach Jonathan on Signal at jwosen.27. Over the past decade, Sanofi and Regeneron’s Dupixent has become the top-selling drug in immunology, bringing in tens of billions in revenue while transforming outcomes for the 1.4 million patients currently on the therapy for conditions including eczema, asthma, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. But investors and doctors are intensely following an experimental therapy positioned to rival the pharma blockbuster, with results from a key study fast approaching. Massachusetts biotech Kymera Therapeutics plans to announce data from a mid-stage clinical trial of its lead asset, KT-621, in eczema before the end of the year. Market analysts for the investment bank Jefferies, using common shorthand for immunology and inflammatory disorders, have called the upcoming results “one of the most impactful I&I readouts this year.” Advertisement Success (or failure) could have major consequences for Kymera, its growing list of competitors, and the millions of people who live with eczema in the United States. The results could also bolster or dampen the biotech’s aspirations to treat a broader class of immunological diseases with its drug, including chronic spontaneous urticaria and asthma. Analysts forecast that the drug’s sales could reach nearly $4 billion by 2035, including more than $3 billion in eczema revenue, according to Visible Alpha. 10月28日，据国家药监局官网显示，嘉兴安帝康生物与先声药业合作开发的1类抗流感创新药玛氘诺沙韦片收到药品通知件，即未能获批上市。图源：NMPA官网玛氘诺沙韦是国内备受关注的抗流感创新药之一。该药最初由安帝康生物自主研发，2023年10月，先声药业与安帝康达成独家合作，获得其在中国地区流感适应症的独家商业化权益。此次上市申报未能顺利推进，也让这款曾被寄予期待的国产抗流感新药，再次成为行业关注的焦点。一、玛氘诺沙韦用药疗程短，单次口服1粒玛氘诺沙韦是一款具有全球自主知识产权的抗流感创新药，属于Cap依赖型核酸内切酶抑制剂。其通过抑制流感病毒Cap依赖型核酸内切酶活性，阻断病毒mRNA转录，从而抑制病毒复制。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库在用药方式上，玛氘诺沙韦的一大特点是疗程短。相关资料显示，成人患者全程仅需单次口服1粒即可完成治疗。相较于需要多次给药的部分抗流感药物，这种给药方式有望提升用药便利性和患者依从性。摩熵医药数据库显示，玛氘诺沙韦于2021年首次申请临床，2025年3月首次申请上市，涉及甲型流感病毒、乙型流感病毒相关适应症。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库从研发到商业化合作，再到上市申请，玛氘诺沙韦的进展也折射出国内抗流感创新药研发的持续推进。二、国产流感新药竞争持续升温玛氘诺沙韦的上市申报遇阻，也让国产抗流感药物的竞争格局再次受到关注。摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库显示，截至目前，国内已有10款流行性感冒新药获批上市。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库2025年便密集迎来了太景生物科技的玛帕西沙韦、征祥医药的玛硒洛沙韦、广东众生药业的昂拉地韦、银杏树药业的玛舒拉沙韦4款国产新药的密集获批上市，让国产抗流感药物正全面驶入爆发期。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库2026年8月13日，上海爱科百发生物医药技术股份有限公司宣布，其自主研发的首款抗流感Fc偶联物（AFC）新药AK0406注射液，用于流感预防适应症的临床试验申请正式获得国家药监局批准。这是中国首个进入临床阶段的流感AFC药物，填补了国内长效抗病毒流感预防领域的技术空白。三、结语随着更多创新药和改良型新药陆续推进，流感治疗领域的竞争正逐渐延伸至作用机制、给药方式及临床应用场景等多个维度。对玛氘诺沙韦而言，后续审评进展及商业化前景仍值得关注。参考来源：[1] Kemny/Science Photo Library By Elaine ChenOct. 27, 2026 National Biotech Reporter Elaine Chen[email protected]Elaine’s stories explore the boom in new obesity treatments, new drug payment models, the ways companies are affected by FDA changes, and the emerging psychedelics drug sector. She co-writes The Readout newsletter, and co-hosts STAT’s weekly biotech podcast, The Readout Loud. You can reach Elaine on Signal at elaineywchen.70. Artiva Biotherapeutics said Tuesday that it’s winding down after two patients died in a trial testing its cell therapy for autoimmune diseases, the latest in a series of safety events that have emerged in a promising research field. One participant in the Phase 2 study died from a neurological complication after receiving the treatment, an NK cell therapy. Researchers determined the death was likely not related to the cell therapy itself, but to a chemotherapy that was given before the cell therapy, Artiva said. It’s standard to give patients chemotherapies before infusing cell therapies to lower the patients’ white blood cell count and make room for the new cells.Advertisement Related Story STAT Plus: Patient dies in Bristol Myers Squibb autoimmune CAR-T trial A second participant experienced sudden death about two months after treatment. Researchers determined that this was not related to any component of the treatment process, but the cause of death has not been determined, the San Diego-based company said. title: Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 19, 2026 Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More Foundayo’s EU backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s masked TCE deal, FDA’s rare disease reset, and Bausch + Lomb’s new interim CEO — explained. Advertisement Lilly’s Foundayo Receives Positive CHMP Opinion for EuropeWhat did the EMA committee recommend?The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended granting marketing authorization in the EU for Foundayo (orforglipron) for two indications: weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, and the treatment of type 2 diabetes in adults whose blood glucose is not adequately controlled. The European Commission makes the final approval decision and typically follows CHMP recommendations within a few weeks.What is Foundayo and why does it matter?Foundayo is Eli Lilly’s oral GLP-1 receptor agonist — a once-daily pill that can be taken at any time of day without food and water restrictions. That last point distinguishes it from other oral GLP-1 therapies currently on the market. The drug received FDA approval for obesity in April 2026 and launched commercially in the United States in the second quarter. Lilly has submitted orforglipron for regulatory review in approximately 40 markets globally.The Stories Covered in this PieceEMA Panel Backs Lilly’s Foundayo for Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes in EuropeFDA Approves Enspryng (Satralizumab) for Thyroid Eye DiseaseAstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 BillionFDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeVir Biotechnology Enters R&D Collaboration with Gilead for Three Novel PRO-XTEN Dual Masked T-Cell EngagersBausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat does this mean competitively?If the European Commission approves Foundayo, it would become the second oral GLP-1 available in the EU for weight management, following Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy pill, which received European approval in July for weight management only. In the type 2 diabetes setting, Foundayo would compete with Novo’s Rybelsus brand of oral semaglutide, which has been on the European market since 2020 and has grown into a multi-billion-dollar franchise. The CHMP recommendation opens a new competitive front between Lilly and Novo Nordisk in Europe’s oral GLP-1 market, adding to their existing rivalry in injectable incretin therapies.What did the clinical evidence show?The weight management recommendation is based on two studies involving more than 4,740 adults with obesity or overweight. The type 2 diabetes recommendation is based on four studies involving 3,765 adults compared against placebo, dapagliflozin, and oral semaglutide.FDA Approves Enspryng for Thyroid Eye DiseaseWhat was approved?The FDA approved Enspryng (satralizumab), an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor developed by Roche, for adults with thyroid eye disease on October 16. Roche describes it as the first subcutaneous therapy for the condition — one that patients or caregivers can administer at home after training from a healthcare provider. It is Enspryng’s second indication; the drug was first approved in 2020 for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.What did the clinical trials show?The approval rests on two identically designed Phase 3 trials, SatraGO-1 and SatraGO-2, which enrolled 258 adults across 19 countries. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with active, moderate-to-severe disease who achieved at least a 2 mm reduction in proptosis — eye bulging — at week 24. Results diverged: SatraGO-2 met its endpoint, with 52.9% of Enspryng-treated patients achieving a proptosis response versus 23.4% on placebo, and 60.7% showing reduced double vision versus 25.8%. SatraGO-1 did not reach statistical significance, with researchers attributing the gap to an unexpectedly high placebo response.How does this change the treatment landscape?Two disease-specific therapies were already approved — Tepezza and, more recently, Lumvoa — both administered by intravenous infusion. Enspryng’s subcutaneous, every-four-week maintenance dosing offers a different treatment experience, with the key benefit being reduced logistical burden rather than a demonstrated efficacy advantage over existing options. No head-to-head comparison with approved therapies was conducted.What are the remaining unknowns?Roche did not disclose pricing or launch timing. Long-term data beyond week 24 were not described in available sources. Separately, the FDA has granted priority review to a supplemental Enspryng application for myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, with a decision expected in January 2027. Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in development and commercial milestones, plus single-digit royalties on global sales.What is insitro’s platform?Insitro’s Virtual Human platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design. The company was founded in 2018 and reports more than $750 million in capital raised, with existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead. It has nine programs in development, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.Why MASH and cardiomyopathies?Both conditions are characterized by disease heterogeneity — a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs — which has complicated treatment development. In MASH, the FDA approved its first treatment, resmetirom (Rezdiffra), in March 2024, but the condition still lacks therapeutic options for most of the estimated 6 to 8 million US patients with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring. The cardiomyopathy scope was not specified in the announcement.What are the limitations of this deal?No drug candidates were named in the announcement. The collaboration sits at the discovery stage, with targets identified through AI-driven analysis still requiring validation through preclinical and clinical work. The $40 million upfront represents less than 3% of the total headline value, and neither company disclosed timelines for milestone payments.FDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeWhat is the Rare Disease Framework Initiative?The FDA announced a new effort to redesign how drugs and biologics for rare diseases are developed and reviewed. The initiative, outlined in a white paper released by the agency’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub, aims to build a regulatory framework tailored to the realities of small patient populations — covering clinical development, evidence standards, manufacturing review, and the role of patient voice throughout the process.Why is FDA doing this now?Despite years of regulatory flexibility programs for rare diseases, only approximately 5% of rare conditions currently have an FDA-approved treatment. The agency says that gap reflects the need for a more fundamentally tailored approach rather than incremental adjustments to a framework originally designed for common diseases.What are the specific commitments?The initiative outlines six priority areas: greater clarity and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance; embedding the patient voice early and at defined milestones; leveraging external expertise for customized review; building shared institutional knowledge; applying risk-based approaches to manufacturing and pre-approval inspections; and championing innovative statistical approaches in rare disease development.What happens next?The FDA is hosting a public meeting on October 28 at its White Oak campus, facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation, to gather input from patients, disease advocates, industry, and other stakeholders. Additional sector-specific roundtables and requests for information will follow. The detailed framework development — which could include new guidance, regulatory changes, and organizational changes within FDA — will be informed by that input.Gilead and Vir Biotechnology Enter $1.87 Billion Masked T-Cell Engager CollaborationWhat are the two companies agreeing to develop?Vir Biotechnology will discover and optimize three novel PRO-XTEN dual-masked T-cell engager development candidates for Gilead, targeting selected solid tumor-associated antigens. Gilead holds an exclusive license to develop, manufacture and commercialize the resulting therapies. Vir will receive $90 million upfront — including $65 million in cash and a $25 million equity investment at a 30% premium — and is eligible for up to $1.74 billion in additional milestones and tiered royalties.What is the PRO-XTEN masking technology?PRO-XTEN is designed to keep T-cell engagers inactive in circulation until they reach the tumor microenvironment, where tumor-specific proteases cleave the mask and activate the drug’s cancer-killing mechanism. That conditional activation is intended to limit systemic toxicity — one of the primary barriers to TCE use in solid tumors — while extending the drug’s half-life and potentially enabling less frequent dosing.Why does this matter for solid tumor oncology?T-cell engagers have proven highly effective in blood cancers but have faced significant limitations in solid tumors, where toxicity and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment have constrained clinical use. Vir’s PRO-XTEN approach directly targets those barriers. This is the second major PRO-XTEN collaboration — an earlier $1.7 billion deal with Astellas for a PSMA-targeted TCE in prostate cancer was announced in February 2026. Together the two deals bring total PRO-XTEN platform value to more than $3.6 billion across two top-tier pharma partners.How does this fit Gilead’s oncology strategy?Today’s deal is Gilead’s third major solid tumor oncology transaction in 2026, following the $5 billion Tubulis ADC acquisition in April and the $2.1 billion Ouro Medicines BCMA T-cell engager acquisition in March. Gilead is simultaneously building in ADCs, T-cell engagers for autoimmune disease, and now masked T-cell engagers for solid tumors — a deliberate multi-mechanism oncology buildout executed across a single year.Bausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat happened at Bausch + Lomb?Bausch + Lomb announced that Brent Saunders departed as CEO by mutual agreement, with Thomas J. Appio named interim CEO effective immediately. Appio, who will retain his role as CEO of parent company Bausch Health, steps into the position just weeks before the company reports third-quarter results and updates its full-year guidance on October 28.What does the company expect for 2026?Simultaneously with the leadership announcement, both Bausch + Lomb and Bausch Health said they expect to raise their full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance based on preliminary third-quarter results, citing strong business performance and anticipated momentum through year-end.What was Saunders building?Saunders returned to Bausch + Lomb in March 2023 — his second stint as CEO — and spent three years stabilizing the company’s supply chain, accelerating commercial execution, and rebuilding its R&D pipeline. He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. After months of anticipation, the Food and Drug Administration gave tentative approval to Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories to make a generic version of a groundbreaking HIV prevention medicine, a key step in widening access for dozens of low- and middle-income countries. The company, one of the world’s largest generic drugmakers, plans to start shipping the medicine next month as part of an effort propelled, in part, by several global health organizations to ensure the drug becomes available in lower-income countries as quickly as possible. The annual cost per person will be $40, comparable to daily tablets.Advertisement Known as lenacapavir, the injectable drug is widely seen as a game-changing tool for eradicating HIV because it offers virtually complete protection against contracting the virus with just one administration every six months. The brand-name version, which is known as Yetzugo in the U.S., is marketed by Gilead Sciences and was approved by the FDA last year. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account? WASHINGTON – Democrats’ landslide victory in the midterm elections may have significant implications for the upcoming negotiations over a key funding source for the Food and Drug Administration in part by empowering a major critic of the program. The FDA collects user fees from pharmaceutical companies to fund the agency’s reviews of their medicines. The Prescription User Fee Drug Act must be renewed before the current law expires on Sept. 30. Otherwise, it could disrupt the FDA’s ability to approve medicines.Advertisement The power to shape that legislation will fall to senior Democrats, including Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT), who is likely to lead the Senate’s health committee. Sanders is one of the few lawmakers who have opposed the core premise of the user fee structure. content: An article from News roundup UniQure gets an FDA decision date; Teva scraps brain drug study The FDA appears likely to hold an advisory committee for UniQure’s closely watched Huntington’s disease gene therapy. Elsewhere, a biotech’s share price was cut in half following a regulatory setback. Published Nov. 3, 2026 By BioPharma Dive staff Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Getty Images Today, a brief rundown of news involving UniQure and Bridge Minds Biosciences, as well as updates from Specific Biologics, Teva Pharmaceuticals and CinRx Pharma that you may have missed. Following a high-profile back and forth with UniQure, the Food and Drug Administration has agreed to review an approval application for the company’s Huntington’s disease gene therapy. UniQure said Monday the agency is doing a faster-than-usual review and should have a verdict by May 1. The FDA is also tentatively planning to discuss the application in a meeting with external advisors, according to UniQure. Though company shares had fallen 7% by late Monday, Wall Street analysts generally viewed the update as positive for what could be the first disease-modifying treatment for Huntington’s. Joseph Thome, of TD Cowen, wrote in a note to clients that his team expects key doctors in the field to adopt the therapy. The proposed trial is designed to evaluate ascending doses of “BMB-101” — which is meant to activate select receptors that, in turn, inhibit certain channel proteins involved in seizures. According to the medication’s developer, New York-based Bright Minds Biosciences, the primary reason the FDA gave for the partial hold was toxicity identified in mouse testing. Bright Minds said the partial hold does not affect its other ongoing trials. The company also said it believes the mouse findings were “incidental and not drug-related,” and that this toxicity was not seen in any other species. Bright Minds plans to “immediately” request further clarification from the FDA. Company shares lost more than half of their value Monday, closing at $26.20 apiece. — Jacob Bell Specific Biologics, a Toronto-based developer of gene editing therapies, announced on Monday the closing of a Series A funding round led by Hatteras Venture Partners. Specific said the $35 million haul was greater than originally planned, and saw participation from half a dozen other investors, including a life sciences venture fund managed by the Business Development Bank of Canada. Teva will evaluate the data before determining the path forward for enrusolmin. In a Monday announcement, the two said they’ve formed a joint venture named CinRock Pharma that’ll advance a pair of experimental drugs that inhibit so-called ROCK2 enzymes. CinRock will test those drugs in pulmonary arterial hypertension, a form of heart failure and other unnamed cardiovascular conditions. title: Corxel, an obesity drugmaker, to go public via SPAC deal
content: An article from Dive Brief // Obesity drugs Corxel, an obesity drugmaker, to go public via SPAC deal Armed with a $300 million financing and two GLP-1 and amylin-targeting medicines, Corxel is set to become the latest weight loss-focused company to join the public markets. Published Oct. 26, 2026 Gwendolyn Wu Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Corxel U.S. will go public via a merger with the SPAC Amanat Acquisition Corp., the companies announced Oct. 26, 2026. Michael Santiago/Getty Images via Getty Images Dive Brief: Corxel Pharmaceuticals, a drug startup developing a pair of weight loss medicines, announced Monday plans to go public by merging with a special purpose acquisition company. The SPAC deal and concurrent $300 million private investment will help Corxel take CX11, a GLP-1 pill licensed from the Chinese drug developer Vincentage Pharma, into late-stage testing. In June, Corxel said CX11 helped participants in a U.S. Phase 2 trial lose an average of up to 11.5% of their body weight after 36 weeks while displaying a “favorable” gastrointestinal tolerability profile. The combined company will also advance a preclinical weight loss prospect directed at a different gut hormone known as amylin. A third drug licensed from Biogen and in development for acute ischemic stroke isn't part of the deal and will instead be housed in a parent entity. Corxel's backers made clear in subsequent talks that they wanted the company to have a "more dedicated focus," rather than pursue "two different tracks," said Kevin Xie, its chief financial officer, in an interview with BioPharma Dive. What followed was a split, with two obesity drugs being merged into a publicly traded entity and the rest of Corxel funneled into a still-private parent. “Both companies have separate development strategies and financing processes, so that’s more welcome news to the investors,” Xie said. Formerly known as Ji Xing Pharmaceuticals, Corxel launched in 2019 and once planned to develop a nasal spray for dry eye disease. It offloaded that therapy in 2024, the same year it acquired from Biogen most rights to JX10 and licensed CX11 from Vincentage. CX11 was already in human testing when Corxel struck that deal. Now it’s on the verge of a global late-stage study. Corxel reported positive late-stage data in May from a Chinese trial run by Vincentage. An international Phase 3 test could follow as soon as the first quarter of 2027. Corxel is pitching CX11 as a “differentiated, next-generation” therapy and an option for people who don’t stay on injectable GLP-1s. Though it is well behind first-to-market oral GLP-1s like Eli Lilly’s Foundayo and Novo’s Wegovy pill, Xie said CX11 may be appealing to people who need to lose 5% to 10% of their body weight and are classified as overweight, but not obese. (Around 31% of U.S. adults fit this description, according to one National Institutes of Health estimate.) Corxel is testing higher doses of CX11 in a Phase 1b trial in an effort to explore the drug’s “efficacy upside,” according to a statement. Additional data are expected in the first half of 2027.
